processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching; this is the parent process (proc_st-1100c-10min-oq) of the aged sample.
Solution-treated samples were aged at temperatures between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h followed by water quenching; this is the 525 °C / 1 h terminal state defining the sample.

structures.overall_structure: α (BCC) matrix containing a large amount of densely precipitated fine α-Mn particles, with only minimal formation of β-Mn after aging the 15Al alloy at 525 °C for 1 h.

phases_present.morphology: fine particles densely dispersed in the α matrix
minimal formation (short rod-shaped, along α grain boundaries and interior)

precipitates.distribution: densely dispersed as fine particles within the α matrix

structures.overall_structure: Single α (Body-centered cubic, BCC) phase formed in the solution-treated Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steel (baseline before aging).

measurement_conditions.test_standard: Vickers hardness (HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester), load 9.8 N for 15 s
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Each sample repeatedly tested 5 times; hardness given as average of 5 measurements.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times; hardness given as average of 5 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the hardness of the 15Al alloy after aging at 525 °C for 1 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 15Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 1 h reached 379.8 ± 19.1 HV, only a slight increase from the 253.4 HV solution-treated baseline.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol); main field 50 μm scale bar, 10 μm inset
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn and β-Mn) in the aged 15Al alloy
characterization_methods.key_findings: In the 525 °C − 1 h SE panel dark needle/plate-like α-Mn and β-Mn particles are visible in an α matrix, consistent with dense fine α-Mn precipitation and minimal β-Mn at this condition.

unmapped_findings: The EDS-measured chemical composition of the 15Al alloy (the base alloy of this sample) is Fe 44.6, Mn 35.2, Al 15.0, Cu 5.2 (at.%) per Table 1 — this is alloy-level (alloy_fe-35mn-15al-5cu) rather than a sample-specific measurement.

The 525 °C/1 h aging condition produced only a small hardening effect in the 15Al alloy (from 253.4 HV solution-treated to 379.8 HV); the paper attributes this to the limited hardening effect of α-Mn, since at this low-temperature short-time aging a large amount of α-Mn precipitated densely while β-Mn formation was minimal.

The ultra-high specific hardness of 141 HV·cm³/g (and the K_IC of 8.6 MPa·m^1/2 with crack length 18 μm, E = 164 GPa) reported for the 15Al alloy corresponds to the peak-hardness condition (965.6 HV, achieved at 600 °C for 6 h), NOT to this 525 °C/1 h sample, so it is excluded here.

The EBSD/TEM characterization of the 15Al alloy detailed in the paper corresponds to other aging conditions (525 °C/3 h, 550 °C/6 h, 650 °C/3 h, and 600 °C/6 h), not to this 525 °C/1 h sample; the only dedicated microstructure data for the 525 °C/1 h condition is the SE-SEM panel in Fig. 7 and the accompanying description in b0045.
